CausalChain: HCC upregulates FASN for de novo lipogenesis → Excess lipid synthesis supports membrane production and survival → Downregulation of fatty acid oxidation further promotes lipid accumulation and reduces ROS generation untowardly → Activation of PPARα can stimulate fatty acid oxidation → Combining FASN inhibition with PPARα activation disrupts lipid supply while increasing oxidative stress → Metabolic overload and increased ROS trigger apoptosis
Hypothesis: In hepatocellular carcinoma, simultaneous inhibition of de novo lipogenesis (e.g., via FASN inhibitors) and activation of fatty acid oxidation (via PPARα agonists) will synergistically induce metabolic stress, leading to enhanced tumor cell apoptosis and reduced tumor growth.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by a profound reprogramming of lipid metabolism, marked by upregulation of de novo lipogenesis and a simultaneous reduction in fatty acid oxidation. This imbalance contributes to the rapid proliferation and survival of malignant cells by supplying essential lipids for membrane biogenesis and regulating apoptotic thresholds. In this context, we propose a dual-modality therapeutic strategy that combines the inhibition of fatty acid synthase (FASN) with pharmacologic activation of peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor alpha (PPARα) to boost fatty acid oxidation. The anticipated outcome is a forced metabolic shift that diminishes the anabolic supply of lipids while concurrently increasing oxidative stress and re‐sensitizing tumor cells to cell death. This testable hypothesis offers a novel integrative approach to disrupt the metabolic plasticity of HCC and may also modulate the tumor microenvironment by reducing lipid‐mediated immunosuppression.
